executionPlan: Implemented progress.ts (versioned record, guarded storage, in-memory fallback) and challenge.ts (cell collection by proximity, beacon gating) on top of the existing session, interaction and animator systems; added three cells and the beacon item to the campus layout, instanced cell and beam visuals sharing the world's neon-cyan material, a lighting pulse in WorldView, the existing dance gesture as the celebration, HUD counter and guidance, Restart in the pause menu and a completion panel. Verified with unit tests, a keyboard-only real-GPU Chrome loop on the dev server (with and without blocked storage), a pause-during-celebration check, and a production build in a copy for the regression.
summary: The challenge and versioned progress are implemented and the full loop (Play, three cells, beacon celebration, completion panel, Restart, reload persistence, Exit) ran in headless Chrome on the real GPU at 1440x900 with the keyboard, also with localStorage blocked. Production regression passed (tower passage sweeps inside 0 and occluded 0, hero gap max 27 ms, rAF p95 16.8 ms, / First Load JS 125 kB, Exit focus on Play); typecheck, lint, test (617 passed) and build all exit 0.

criteria.criterion: Challenge: one energy cell near each destination, each reachable on foot and visible from its approach, each collectible once (collecting twice counts once), an accessible HUD counter 'Energy cells n/3' with a polite live-region announcement, guidance back to the plaza after the third (a visible cue plus text), and interacting with the beacon only after all three triggers a short lighting effect and a celebration (the existing celebration-style gesture or clip on the avatar, no new external asset unless recorded in ASSETS.md) followed by a completion panel with Explore more, View projects and Contact actions; challenge.test.ts covers uniqueness, beacon gating, completion and restart.
criteria.evidence: Layout: one cell per destination (lab, workshop, tower) 2.0 to 2.6 m inside the door or passage on the approach axis; challenge.test.ts (15 tests) checks one cell per destination near it, a walkable surface at the cell height with open space above, collection within radius and floor only, collecting twice counts once and notifies once, nothing collected outside playing, beacon unfocused and inert before the third cell, focus plus E after it starts celebrating and saves completion, completion panel then close to playing, no second activation, restart then replay. Browser: cell visible through the Lab door from outside (out/1-cell-approach.png), counter 'Energy cells n/3' in a role=status aria-live=polite region (challengeUi.test.tsx asserts it), guidance chip plus a tall cyan beam over the beacon after the third cell (out/3-guidance.png), celebration plays the existing public/animations/dance.glb gesture for 3.6 s with a cyan lighting pulse (out/4-celebration.png; no new asset, ASSETS.md row updated), then the completion panel with Explore more, View projects and Contact (out/5-completion.png; challengeUi.test.tsx covers the three actions). Deviation from design 2.9: the beacon shows no prompt (and no touch Interact button) before the third cell; the counter carries that information.

criteria.criterion: Progress: progress is saved locally in a versioned format; reload restores collected cells and completion; Restart in the pause menu clears challenge progress but keeps settings; corrupt JSON, wrong types, an unknown version and a throwing storage getter fall back safely (in-memory when storage is unavailable, with no error to the visitor); progress.test.ts covers each case; in the browser with storage blocked the loop still completes.
criteria.evidence: progress.ts versioned record (version 1, key portfolio.game.progress, ADR-005). progress.test.ts (36 tests): round trip, 19 invalid inputs (corrupt JSON, empty string, array, number, null, missing/string/fractional/0/newer version, wrong types, unknown cell, completed without 3 cells, missing settings, bad volume/quality/reducedMotion) all give the default with status invalid; throwing storage getter, throwing getItem, absent storage and setItem quota error all fall back to memory with persistent false and no throw; restart keeps settings. Browser (loop.json): reload restored 3/3 and completed true; Restart from the pause menu gave 0/3 with settings kept; one cell then reload gave 1/3. Storage blocked (blocked.json, localStorage getter throws SecurityError): loop completed 0/3 to completion panel, Restart worked, no error text, errs []. Not testable: the n -> n+1 migration loop has no shipped older version to exercise (only unknown-version rejection is tested).

assumptions: The two programs compiled at the first game frame in the production run (avaturn_hair_0_material and a depth program) are not caused by the cells (the cell and beam meshes share the neon-cyan program and are in the warm-up probes); I did not build a base-commit control to prove they pre-exist, so that is an inference from the program list.

The celebration is capped at 3.6 s of the 5.2 s dance clip, and skipped to a 1.0 s lighting-only beat under reduced motion; a pause during the celebration skips the rest and opens the completion panel on Resume (verified in the browser), unless Restart cleared the completion.
A stored record with completed true but fewer than three cells is treated as invalid (reset to default), a small tightening of ADR-005 (which lists wrong shapes as invalid).
createGame with an explicit storage option gets its own store; without it the page-wide singleton is used so progress survives Exit and re-entry within a visit.
Beacon is focusable only when ready (3 cells and not completed); after completion it stays inert until Restart.
decisionsProposed: ADR-005 addendum: a record with completed true and fewer than three cells is invalid; createGame(storage) bypasses the singleton for tests.

Integration point for the touch stage: game.focus (already passed to TouchControls) now holds the beacon item only when it can be activated, so the context-sensitive Interact button shows exactly then; cells never take focus (proximity collection).
lessonsProposed: A third-person camera with free orbit stays where it is when the player walks back toward it, so a wide beam or prop between the camera and the avatar can hide the avatar; keep celebration props thin and recentre the camera (R) in browser scripts before screenshots.

When counting shader programs at the first game frame, list the cache keys of programs added after the swap before blaming a new mesh: here the two late programs were the hair material and a depth program.
